structure.title: Delegated authority
structure.text: The Duke withdraws from public rule and leaves Angelo to enforce laws that have long been loosely observed.

structure.title: Private demands and public judgment
structure.text: A plea for mercy becomes a test of the deputy's integrity. Hidden observation and unequal knowledge complicate every attempted remedy.

people.name: Angelo
people.text: The cold, upright deputy left in charge of Vienna, who revives a forgotten law and sentences a young man to death for fornication.

people.name: Isabella
people.text: A young woman about to enter a convent, who comes to plead with Angelo for her brother's life.

people.name: Claudio
people.text: Isabella's brother, condemned to die for getting his betrothed pregnant before their marriage was formally made.

context.title: Discretion in law
context.text: A law's existence does not explain when or how it should be enforced. Sudden severity changes the risks of familiar conduct.
context.takeaway: Compare legality with consistency and justice.

context.title: Reputation and evidence
context.text: Respectability makes some speakers easier to believe than others. The possibility of complaint depends on more than telling the truth.
context.takeaway: Ask who can make an accusation heard.

notice.text: Notice the Duke's management of information.
notice.why: Observing wrongdoing and arranging justice are different responsibilities.

opening: A ruler puts his morally rigorous deputy in charge of a city accustomed to ignoring its own laws. When the deputy sentences a young man to death, the man's sister comes to plead for him. Her appeal awakens a desire the official has no intention of applying his principles to honestly. Shakespeare places a woman with almost no public power before a man whose reputation makes him difficult to accuse, exposing what happens when the authority to punish comes with control over whose story will be believed.
